verdict: Wix: Choose Wix when the website and brand pages are the product — and ecommerce is a first-class but secondary job on the same builder. Scores use the Ecommerce editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: Fast website + store launch for design-led SMBs
Clear ecommerce plan gate at Core
Integrated bookings/marketing for service + product mixes
weaknesses: Not a Shopify peer for complex commerce ops
bestFor: SMBs that need a polished website and a store in one builder
Service businesses adding light product sales
Founders prioritizing design speed over commerce OS depth
notIdealFor: High-SKU catalogs, heavy B2B, or marketplace ops
Retailers whose center of gravity is POS hardware
Teams that need open-source code ownership
tradeoffs: Subscription floors vs payment-processing spreads and GMV/overage fees
App/extension TCO vs native feature depth
Open-source/hosting flexibility vs SaaS operational simplicity
Dropshipping product caps vs catalog automation depth
recommendation: Choose Wix when the website and brand pages are the product — and ecommerce is a first-class but secondary job on the same builder. Consider Squarespace for design-led peers; Shopify for commerce-first SaaS; WooCommerce if you already live in WordPress.
editorialNotes: Ecommerce Priority-1 batch. Approved on ecommerce-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=website-builder. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Drag-and-drop editor is the product strength — merchants launch sites without developers.
Primary job is website + store together; scored as website-builder commerce, not a full commerce OS.
Solid for SMB catalogs; weaker for complex B2B and multi-warehouse depth.
Payments unlock on Core+; conversion tooling exists but trails Shop Pay-class ecosystems.
App Market and native payments/channels cover SMB needs — not Magento-scale extensibility.
Limited retail POS story versus Square Online.
Business Elite helps, but high-GMV complex catalogs usually outgrow website-builder packaging.
Core/Business annual tiles are competitive for site+store SMBs when design speed matters.
Wix AI assists design and copy — useful, secondary to the builder job.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine ecommerce editorial criteria using category weights (storefront/commerce fit 15, catalog/orders 14, ease 12, checkout 12, integrations 12, value 12, omnichannel/POS 10, scalability 9, AI 6), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — SaaS platforms, open-source carts, omnichannel POS bundles, and dropshipping sourcing apps are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score; affiliate economics are excluded.
